submitter: bugs_open/328 lane — outbound suppression of links to never-shipped pages (round 1)
rationale: bugs_open/328: a page that fails to build stays linked from the pages that did, so one blocked page becomes a visibly broken site. STILL LIVE, re-measured 2026-08-23 cache-busted: https://loanzy.uk/ serves 200 carrying href="/your-rights.html" x2 and href="/guides/index.html" x1, both 404. It REPRODUCES ON A BUILD THAT RAN THAT DAY: loanzy redeployed all 17 pages 13:13-14:24Z and the home page shipped at 13:28:27Z, at which instant your-rights (needs_rebuild, deployed_at NULL) and guides-index (planned, deployed_at NULL) had been untouched since 2026-08-18 with no open work item. The information was unambiguous in the pages table at render time and nothing consulted it. THE HOLE: datahelpers.RepairPageLinks already unlinks dead in-body links at four seams, and all four load their index from ONE function, loadValidPagePaths (validate_page_content.go:1515), whose query is `SELECT url FROM pages WHERE site_id=$1 AND status NOT IN ('deleted','archived')` -- NO build-axis arm at all. A page row that has never existed on the web is a perfectly good link target to every one of them. The identical omission was fixed on three sibling loaders on 2026-08-09 (resolve_internal_links_action.go:862-899); this loader was missed. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE BUG FILE, both measured. (1) Its 2026-08-21 contrib says the work items 'sit at needs_human_review with no handler ... parked unread'. The rows say otherwise: all 58 parked items carry triaged_at, handler_agent='page-build-handler' and attempt_count>=1 -- dispatched, attempted, FAILED (48 'no sections ready to build', 10 'content validation failed'). The type implements ONE remedy, build the target, and on this population that remedy is unavailable by construction. bugs_open/220's routing is not the gap. (2) The open-item count overstates live harm ~3x: 42 of the 63 name targets that serve HTTP 200 today (the 40 lendzy items, gaswholesalers fuel-pricing-framework, mortgagecalculator contact/index) -- stale records held open by missing deployed_at stamps, the bugs_open/315 family. The honest harm is the blast-radius number: 36 anchors on 24 deployed pages pointing at 14 unservable targets across 9 sites. THE PREDICATE IS A NEW FAMILY MEMBER AND NEITHER EXISTING ONE WOULD DO, measured not argued. NeverDeployedPagePredicate selects 9 pages that return HTTP 200 today -- delisting a working page is 'worse than the bug' (bugs_open/052). PageMayBeLinkedPredicateFor's planned-only floor still holds (17/17 of those rows 404) but MISSES the three needs_rebuild rows that were never built at all, 3/3 returning 404, one of which is this bug's own instance. The discriminator is the rendered-component count, and it separates the mixed class exactly: 20 never-shipped pages with ZERO rendered components returned 404, 20 of 20; 9 with at least one returned 200, 9 of 9. The conjunction is load-bearing -- 8 pages fleet-wide have deployed_at set AND zero components (served by another subsystem, a tool or a blog index), so a component test alone would delist all eight; the never-deployed arm excludes them first. The 48h staleness clock on the planned arm is what tells 'not coming' from 'not yet', and a time threshold is tolerable ONLY because the consequence is bounded: suppression is OUTBOUND-ONLY and recomputed every render, so a wrongly refused target restores itself on the referrer's next render with nothing lost. WHY OUTBOUND-ONLY IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. Nothing here touches content_data. The authored href survives in the source the platform re-renders from, so the day the target ships the anchor returns by itself -- no cascade, no repair queue, no second mechanism that has to keep pace, which is what separates 328 from 079/097 whose targets genuinely do not exist and are correctly repaired at source. It also means check_phantom_internal_links, which reads STORED rendered_html, still sees the authored anchor: this change silences no detector, and every suppression additionally writes its own CONTENT_LINK_SUPPRESSED_UNSHIPPED row naming the hrefs. TWO ARMS, BECAUSE THE MARKUP HAS TWO SHAPES. There is a standing LANDMINE on the sibling unlink arm: a dead link is 'REPAIRED into orphaned prose ... where the anchor's inner content is the link LABEL -- which is every card, CTA and read-more control on this platform -- the served page shows the label and the arrow glyph as bare text in the middle of the card'. I sampled all 36 affected anchors rather than assuming: 28 are classless prose anchors inside a sentence, 8 are classed template controls whose inner content is a short label plus an arrow. So prose unlinks (keep the words) and a control is dropped WHOLE -- DropDeadURLControls' own rule for chrome, LNK-005 correct-or-absent -- on the OWNER'S EXPLICIT DECISION of 2026-08-23. The control arm requires class= AND stripped inner text <=60 chars, so an ambiguous anchor falls back to unlink, the fail-safe direction link_repair.go names for a writer. RFC_010 SEC 2 COMPLIANCE, and it is why this is NOT a widening of loadValidPagePaths. That one loader feeds four seams with different write surfaces, including the persistence chokepoint that writes BOTH page_components.rendered_html AND content_data; teaching it about deployment would change all four in one edit. So the new authority is a separate, strictly narrower set consumed only at the two outbound seams, behind an opt-in step-config field suppress_unshipped_links whose UNSAFE side (the writer that removes an anchor) is the DEFAULT-OFF one. The four consumers of loadValidPagePaths are named in grounded_in and NOTHING about their guarantee changes (owner ruling 2026-07-29 sec 3). A source scan asserts the suppression is unreachable from any persistence seam, because a comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share. I DECLARE THE OBJECTION RATHER THAN WAIT FOR IT: the concept register's LNK-030 carries a standing architecture-seat advisory that a cross-cutting eligibility decision answered twice by hand-rolled predicates (CLC-013, LNK-030) is 'a candidate RFC subject ... Do not treat LNK-030 as closing the class.' THIS WOULD BE THE THIRD INSTANCE. The mitigation is real but PARTIAL: no third spelling of the judgement is introduced -- the predicate joins the existing family in datahelpers/links.go with the family's own alias/parenthesisation tests, and the policy type is LNK-030's shape reused point for point including both degrade escapes. It does NOT close the class, and I am flagging that for the architecture seat rather than claiming it does. LNK-030 also records that tightening the content path was deferred as needing 'a separate, fleet-wide, measured change' because it 'would strip CTAs from most of every fresh build and redefine the unresolved_cta HITL signal'. That deferral is about loadResolverPageSet, the CTA resolver's CANDIDATE set -- where a CTA is sent. This change touches none of loadResolverPageSet, loadContentHubs, loadInteractivePages or unresolved_cta; it acts on assembled HTML after every resolver has had its say. The fleet-wide measurement that paragraph asks for is the one in grounded_in, and the deferral's stated cost does not materialise: 3,193 anchors kept vs 36 suppressed (1.1%), and on loanzy's real build the rule would have removed exactly the two dead links and nothing else. THE DRAIN (edits 6-7) is separable but belongs here: the type has 72 items in its whole history and ZERO ever closed, because it is born needs_human_review and CompleteWorkItemAction's status guard refuses to leave that status, so the registered completion verifier can never run. Registering it in reviewRevalidators delegates to the SAME function the completion gate runs, so the drain and the gate cannot answer differently. It will honestly report still_holds on the ~42 items whose targets serve 200 with a NULL deployed_at -- that is the 315 stamping gap, reported not papered over. TESTS ARE MUTATION-PROVEN, NOT MERELY GREEN, and two of them FAILED that proof first and were rewritten: the default-OFF test was vacuous (with no query registered, the flag-ON mutant fell through the fail-open branch and produced identical output, so it passed on the mutant) and the seam source scan matched 'name(' so a mutant taking the function as a VALUE walked past it. Both fixed and re-proven. Five mutants now die for the right reasons; details in grounded_in.

plan.summary: bugs_open/328: a deployed page keeps serving anchors to pages of its own site that have never shipped, because the estate's one link-repair index has no build-axis arm. Adds a fourth, measured member to the datahelpers predicate family; a two-armed suppression pass in its own file (unlink prose, drop a labelled control whole); a chrome-policy-shaped loader with the same two degrade escapes; wires it at the TWO outbound seams (one of which was entirely unprotected) behind an opt-in step-config field defaulting OFF; and registers the never-drained work-item type with the same verifier the completion gate runs. Nothing writes to content_data, so the authored href survives and the anchor returns by itself when the target ships.

edits.rationale: Adds PageLinkRefusedPredicateFor to the build-axis predicate family -- the ONE home for 'would an anchor here 404 and is the page not arriving'. No second spelling is introduced anywhere. The alias is REQUIRED and the bare form degrades to FALSE (suppress nothing) rather than to a predicate that would refuse every page: the correlated subquery's unqualified `id` would bind to page_components.id inside the EXISTS, which is always true. The doc comment carries the dated measurement, the per-domain control that saved it, and why neither existing sibling is correct.
edits.sketch:
+// PageLinkRefusedPredicateFor is the OUTBOUND-SUPPRESSION floor ... 20 never-shipped
+// pages with zero rendered components returned 404, 20 of 20; 9 with at least one
+// returned 200, 9 of 9 (measured 2026-08-23, per-domain 404 control).
+func PageLinkRefusedPredicateFor(alias string) string {
+	if alias == "" { return "FALSE" }
+	q := alias + "."
+	return fmt.Sprintf(
+		"( (%[1]sdeployed_at IS NULL AND COALESCE(%[1]sbuild_status,'') = 'planned'"+
+		" AND %[1]supdated_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '%[2]d hours')"+
+		" OR (%[1]sdeployed_at IS NULL AND COALESCE(%[1]sbuild_status,'') = 'needs_rebuild'"+
+		" AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM page_components pc"+
+		" WHERE pc.page_id = %[1]sid AND COALESCE(pc.rendered_html,'') <> '')) )",
+		q, PlannedPageRefusedAfterHours)
+}

edits.rationale: The pass, in its OWN FILE per link_repair.go's own rule that a behaviour change must not arrive as a passenger on an edit to the shared vocabulary. Two arms measured from the real markup (28 prose / 8 control). Reuses repairAnchorRe, MarkupMatches (the bugs_open/180 script/comment mask -- load-bearing here because BOTH arms delete markup and the control arm deletes a whole element), HasRuntimeFillMarker whole-input (the writer-direction argument), normaliseAnchorText (so 'what the link says' has one definition) and ClassifyLinkScope. Empty/nil set is a byte-identical no-op. Ships with link_suppress_test.go: mixed batch with a positive control in the SAME document, the control/prose split, the fallback, the runtime-fill exemption, the script-quoted anchor, and normalisation parity.

The site-level policy, deliberately a SIBLING of chrome_link_policy.go: same shape, same two degrade escapes, same fail directions. loadRefusedLinkTargets returns (nil,false) on a failed lookup, on a scan error, on a truncating row error, AND when the site has ZERO shipped pages -- the first-build escape, which keys on the SHIPPED-PAGE COUNT and never on the size of the refused set (reading emptiness as the first-build signal is the mistake chrome_link_policy.go records being caught by a test). suppressUnshippedOutboundLinks reads the opt-in via configBoolOrDefault(..., false), and writes a durable CONTENT_LINK_SUPPRESSED_UNSHIPPED row naming every href -- a FOURTH code beside the three existing ones, for the reason save_sections_content_data_links.go gives for being distinct: 'the target does not exist' and 'the target exists and has never shipped' want opposite follow-up actions. A skip writes writeLinkRepairSkipLog, because a pod log line is not a record.
edits.sketch:
+rows, err := db.QueryContext(ctx, `
+	SELECT p.url,
+	       `+datahelpers.PageLinkRefusedPredicateFor("p")+` AS refused,
+	       `+datahelpers.PageHasShippedPredicateFor("p")+` AS shipped
+	FROM pages p WHERE p.site_id = $1 AND p.`+linkablePageStatusPredicate, siteID)
+...
+if shippedPages == 0 {
+	logger.Warn("link suppression: site has NO shipped pages — outbound links go UNSUPPRESSED ...")
+	return nil, false
+}
+...
+if !configBoolOrDefault(params.StepConfig.Config, suppressUnshippedLinksKey, false) { return html }

edits.rationale: Outbound seam 1. ONE call covers three publish paths: both rerender paths (rerender_single_page_action.go:223, rerender_pages_actions.go:214) AND the initial build, because page-build-handler's deploy_page is a call_agent with target_role 'page_renderer' which is the page-rerender agent (archived_page_guard.go:38 states the mapping). It runs on the REPAIRED string, not the original: the rewrite arm above can turn '/your-rights' into the stored '/your-rights.html', and the refused set holds stored pages.url values, so judging the pre-repair string would miss exactly the anchors the repair just normalised. The early return for 'no repairs' also had to route through it, or a page with no dead links would skip suppression entirely.

edits.rationale: Outbound seam 2, and the one a single-seam design would have missed: AssemblePageAction injects chrome and returns the page HTML calling NEITHER repairOutboundPageLinks NOR RepairPageLinks. It is the initial-build/loop path -- enumerated live and recursively on 2026-08-23 (a top-level jsonb_each MISSES these, they are nested in sub_workflows): pageflow-builder, page-rebuild and site-work-orchestrator. Placed after chrome injection so the whole outbound string is judged, matching what the rerender seam already does, and immediately before the return so it is the last thing that touches the bytes. Degrades to a no-op when site_record.site_id is absent or unparseable.

The queue drain the type has never had. CLOSER CENSUS, the bar this map's earlier adopters set after one lane shipped a duplicate closer: 72 rows in the type's whole history, ZERO ever complete or verified, count(DISTINCT resolution_path)=0, only 3 carrying a _verification stamp. ONE producer, check_phantom_internal_links.go. Same birth-status trap as truncated_component. It DELEGATES to checks.VerifyUnbuiltInternalLinkResolved -- the same function complete_work_item runs -- so the drain and the gate cannot answer the same question differently, and it resolves the target page from spec.target_page_id (which the producing check writes) rather than widening the shared parkedReviewItem loader. Confusing that with spec.page_id, the page CONTAINING the link, was bugs_open/220's entire mechanism, so the two are named apart at every mention. It retracts and rewrites nothing; an error is `unknown`, non-terminal.

Registers the drain, which is also what widens what the sweep LOADS (coveredItemTypes derives from this map, so the two cannot disagree). The deliberate coverage ratchet in revalidate_review_queue_test.go fired on this addition exactly as designed -- 'if that is deliberate, update this test and say why in the commit' -- and is updated in the same edit with the closer census written into the test's own comment, matching what the four earlier adopters did.

The CONFIG half, held back from the runner because the Go is inert until the roll and applying early would make the fix LOOK live when it is not. Turns the opt-in on at the four live seam steps and DELIBERATELY LEAVES report-builder OFF (report pages were not in the census; turning it on later is one UPDATE, turning it on now would be an unmeasured claim). The six live paths were enumerated RECURSIVELY on 2026-08-23 because three are nested in sub_workflows and a top-level jsonb_each misses them; page-rerender.rerender_sections is named and explained as NOT a seam (its action writes sections and always flows onward to render_page, where assembly and the repair passes happen) so the next reader need not re-derive it. Guards are DO/RAISE, not SELECTs, because ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result and a SELECT verify cannot stop the COMMIT: $pre$ refuses a drifted path or an already-applied run, $post$ asserts exactly 4 keys ON and asserts report-builder did NOT acquire one. Exact-inverse _ROLLBACK sidecar (#- the one key per path), not a snapshot restore, so it cannot clobber another session's edit to those rows.

grounded_in: LIVE, 2026-08-23, cache-busted: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' 'https://loanzy.uk/?cb=$RANDOM' -> 200; /your-rights.html -> 404; /guides/index.html -> 404; mortgagecalculator.co.uk/scorecard-simulator.html -> 404. And the anchors are still served: curl -s https://loanzy.uk/ | grep -o 'href="[^"]*"' | sort | uniq -c -> `2 href="/your-rights.html"`, `1 href="/guides/index.html"`.

REPRODUCED ON A BUILD THAT RAN THE SAME DAY: SELECT name,url,build_status,deployed_at FROM pages p JOIN sites s ON s.id=p.site_id WHERE s.domain='loanzy.uk' -> all 17 live pages deployed_at between 2026-08-23 13:13:05Z and 14:24:05Z; index (/index.html) at 13:28:27Z; your-rights needs_rebuild/deployed_at NULL/updated_at 2026-08-18 21:29Z; guides-index planned/deployed_at NULL/updated_at 2026-08-18 20:42Z.

THE HANDLER RAN AND FAILED (correction 1): SELECT status, CASE WHEN error ILIKE '%no sections ready to build%' THEN 'no sections ready' WHEN error ILIKE '%content validation failed%' THEN 'validation blockers' ... END, count(*) FROM site_work_items WHERE item_type='unbuilt_internal_link' GROUP BY 1,2 -> needs_human_review/no sections ready = 48; needs_human_review/validation blockers = 10; cancelled = 9; failed = 5. Every parked row carries triaged_at, handler_agent='page-build-handler' and attempt_count >= 1.

DETECTION DID NOT COVER THE MOTIVATING INSTANCE: SELECT item_type,status,left(summary,110) FROM site_work_items w JOIN sites s ON s.id=w.site_id WHERE s.domain='loanzy.uk' AND (summary ILIKE '%your-rights%' OR summary ILIKE '%guides/index%' OR item_type IN ('unbuilt_internal_link','phantom_internal_link')) -> NO unbuilt_internal_link row names /your-rights.html or /guides/index.html; the site's only three name a different page's component (about:about-content). A fix routed through the item queue would miss this bug's own headline case.

THE HTTP CENSUS AND ITS CONTROL, 2026-08-23. All 56 never-shipped pages fetched cache-busted, plus a per-domain control (an invented URL fetched in the same run). adversecreditmortgage.co.uk returns 200 with a 114-byte parked-registrar redirect (`window.location.href="/lander"`) for EVERY path INCLUDING the invented control, so its 19 rows are false 200s and are excluded; two *.internal hosts unreachable. Of the 29 rows that survive: planned+never-deployed 0x200 / 17x404; needs_rebuild+never-deployed with >=1 rendered component 9x200 / 0x404; needs_rebuild+never-deployed with 0 components 0x200 / 3x404. Combined on the component axis: 20 with zero components -> 20/20 404; 9 with >=1 -> 9/9 200. WITHOUT the control the same data reads '19 planned pages serve 200', which refutes the whole approach -- the measurement was disconfirmable and its uncontrolled form DID come out the other way.

THE CONJUNCTION IS LOAD-BEARING: SELECT (deployed_at IS NOT NULL), EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM page_components pc WHERE pc.page_id=p.id AND COALESCE(pc.rendered_html,'')<>''), count(*) FROM pages p WHERE COALESCE(status,'') NOT IN ('deleted','archived') GROUP BY 1,2 -> deployed+no components = 8. A component-count test alone would delist all eight (tool/blog-index pages served by another subsystem, which realisedPageHasShipped already records); the never-deployed arm excludes them first.

BLAST RADIUS, every <a href> in every stored page_components.rendered_html fleet-wide resolved against the predicate (2026-08-23): servable targets -> 3,193 anchor hits / 577 referring pages / 557 targets, UNTOUCHED; unservable -> 36 anchor hits / 24 referring pages / 14 targets, SUPPRESSED. 1.1% of internal anchors, and every one of them is a live 404 today. It also names damage the work-item queue never filed: remortgagecalculator.uk (2 targets, 6 hits), webdesign.co.uk, and both pool-*.internal sites -- 14 targets on 9 sites against the queue's 13 on 7.

THE GREENFIELD OBJECTION, TESTED ON A REAL BUILD RATHER THAN ASSUMED: loanzy's home page carries 10 distinct internal hrefs; 8 of the 10 targets had already deployed (13:13-13:27Z) when it shipped at 13:28:27Z. The rule would have suppressed EXACTLY the two dead links and nothing else. [n=1 on the ordering claim; the 3,193/36 split is the general measurement.]

THE MARKUP SPLIT that decided the two arms (2026-08-23), sampled from the real rendered_html of all 36 affected anchors: 28 are CLASSLESS prose anchors mid-sentence (e.g. `automated intelligence pipeline case study`); 8 are CLASSED template controls (e.g. `Read your rights→`).

CONSUMERS OF loadValidPagePaths, NAMED (owner ruling 2026-07-29 sec 3), and what changes for them: NOTHING. validate_page_content.go:314 (deploy gate), rerender_single_page_action.go:222, component_link_repair.go:101, save_sections_link_repair.go:145 (persistence, writes rendered_html AND content_data). This change adds no arm to that loader and alters no row it returns; the refused set is a separate, strictly narrower query consumed only at the two outbound seams.

RFC_022 CONDITIONS, WITH THE QUERY NOT THE ASSERTION: opt-in yes; unsafe default OFF yes; zero live consumers name it -- SELECT type FROM agent_definitions WHERE is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL AND default_config::text LIKE '%suppress_unshipped_links%' -> 0 rows (2026-08-23).

THE SIX LIVE SEAM PATHS, enumerated RECURSIVELY on 2026-08-23 (a top-level jsonb_each misses three of them): pageflow-builder workflow,steps,build_pages_loop,config,sub_workflow,steps,assemble_page; page-rebuild same path; site-work-orchestrator workflow,steps,build_items_loop,config,sub_workflow,steps,assemble_page; page-rerender workflow,steps,render_page; report-builder workflow,steps,render_page; page-rerender workflow,steps,rerender_sections. page-rerender's own step graph: check_rerender_mode -> rerender_sections -> ... -> save_sections -> render_page -> check_skipped -> deploy_page, so rerender_sections always flows into render_page and needs no key of its own.

Dying correctly now: (a) control arm's class check removed -> TestProseAnchorIsUnlinkedAndTheServableSiblingSurvives FAILS (prose text deleted); (b) MarkupMatches -> raw regex -> TestAnchorQuotedInsideScriptIsNotDeleted FAILS (script string rewritten); (c) runtime-fill exemption removed -> TestRuntimeFillShellIsExempt FAILS; (d) zero-shipped escape deleted -> TestZeroShippedPagesDisablesSuppression FAILS; (e) opt-in default flipped to true -> TestSuppressionIsOffWithoutTheOptIn FAILS; (f) a value-reference added in save_sections_link_repair.go -> TestSuppressionIsConfinedToTheOutboundSeams FAILS.
